# SK7081 — The type depends on more other types than the threshold

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

One type declaration mentions more distinct other named types than dotnet_code_quality.SK7081.threshold (default 80).

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Maintainability |
| Default severity | hint |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 1.3 |
| Supersedes | S1200 |

## Why

This is the metric `SK7001`–`SK7006` do not carry. A type can be short, shallow and simple in every one of them and still know about forty other types, and every one of those forty is a reason this file has to be reopened when something else changes. Counting the distinct named types a declaration mentions — bases, member types, locals, constructions, static receivers, attributes and the arguments of the generics it names — measures how much of the design has to be held in mind at once to change it, which is what people mean when they say a class is entangled. ⚠ The default of 80 is deliberately far above the textbook 30: on Skala's own tree — which is a Roslyn analyzer host, and therefore names one type per syntax-node kind before it does anything — a threshold of 30 fires on 125 type declarations and 80 fires on six, and those six are the god objects a reader would name unprompted. Reporting the shoulder of the distribution rather than its tail is the "useless" outcome this family's rationale names. Splitting a type is a design change with no mechanical form, so there is no fix.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
// one class that names forty other types across its fields, parameters and locals
```

Write:

```csharp
// the same work behind two or three collaborators, each naming its own handful
```

## When it does not fire

A metric rule has no false positives in the sense doc 16 § R3 means: it reports a measurement against a threshold, and the measurement is either right or a bug. What it can be is *useless* — a threshold low enough to fire on ordinary code teaches people to switch the category off — so the default is set above what the reference trees contain and the threshold is an .editorconfig option. ⚠ **Special types are not counted.** `int`, `string`, `object`, `void`, `IEnumerable<T>` and the rest of the language's own vocabulary would add the same handful to every type in the repository and separate nothing. ⚠ **The type itself, anything nesting it, and anything it nests are not counted**: a type that organises itself with nested helpers is not coupled to somebody else's design, and the file a reader opens contains both. ⚠ **A nested type is not descended into** — it has its own declaration and its own measurement, and charging the outer type for the inner one's dependencies would report the same union once per level. ⚠ **An unresolved reference is skipped rather than counted**, which under-reports; on a source slice with no dependency closure (issue #277) it under-reports to nothing, so a zero from this rule on such a tree says the analysis declined and not that the types are decoupled. Measured per *declaration*, like `SK7004`, so a partial type is measured once per file — which is the file a person opens. Generated code is excluded.

## Configuration

- `dotnet_code_quality.SK7081.threshold`
- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK7081.severity`
